# Patches

<!-- bp-patch v0.13: this file is yours; only the table between the markers is regenerated by `bp-patch.sh docs`. -->

## Goal

This fork of TrueGrid fixes problems observed while playing as a non-host client on a friend's listen
server, where the upstream mod misbehaves even though single player works. Each fix is a small,
reviewable change to one Blueprint asset, kept as a patch so it can be re-applied, reviewed, and offered
upstream as a plain `.uasset` change with a readable description of what moved.

## How patches are made

Each folder here is one fix:

- `patch.json`: a [bp-patch](../README.md) patch (format 2), a list of operations on one Blueprint graph.
  Applied headless with `./bp-patch/bp-patch.sh apply <id> ./TrueGrid`, checked offline with `lint`,
  rehearsed in Unreal with `check` (nothing saved).
- `editor.md`: the same change as Unreal Editor instructions (a walkthrough plus a generated checklist).
- `diff.txt`: pseudo-code diff of the Blueprint graphs before and after the patch.
- `README.md`: the write-up: the problem, the original code and why it may have been written that way,
  the fix, risks, status, testing and history.
- `PR.md`: write-up + diff, for an upstream pull request body (generated).

`stack.json` records which patches are in which asset, in order, with hashes of the result; `_pristine/`
holds the unmodified originals the stack is rebuilt from (`./bp-patch/bp-patch.sh rebuild ./TrueGrid`).
Nodes a patch adds carry deterministic GUIDs, so `./bp-patch/bp-patch.sh status ./TrueGrid` can tell
which patches an asset really contains.

Upstream PRs: `./bp-patch/bp-patch.sh rebuild ./TrueGrid --only <id>` makes the asset with just that one
patch for a branch off upstream; `patches/` itself stays in the fork.
